How It Works

Not a chatbot. A full intake system.

Here's exactly what happens — and exactly how — between an enquiry landing and a booked job appearing on your calendar.

01 — Email system

A missing mobile number is never a dead end.

When a genuine enquiry arrives by email without a recognised phone number, Hermia does not leave it sitting in an inbox. It replies through your branded email system and gives the lead a clear way to continue.

The response gathers the missing contact detail, keeps the conversation under your business name, and moves the lead into the same trade-specific qualification flow. A missing number has a next step — not a lost opportunity.

Email route in action
The enquiry is acknowledged and moved into the right next step without waiting for an office inbox to be opened.
02 — Phone / WhatsApp system

A recognised phone number starts a direct conversation.

When an enquiry or sending domain comes through with a recognised phone number, Hermia sends the lead a direct WhatsApp message rather than waiting for a manual reply. The lead can respond on the channel they are most likely to see.

Whether the lead entered through email or phone, every valid enquiry then receives the same structured qualification — so your team gets usable job detail, not a loose message to chase later.

Phone / WhatsApp route in action
Hermia asks for the missing trade detail in the same conversation, so an incomplete answer does not become a job brief.
03 — Aggressive Filtering

Generic answers do not pass.

Hermia does not accept “it’s leaking,” “the roof,” or “there is a defect” as a job brief. It keeps asking trade-specific follow-up questions until the issue is specific enough for your team to act on.

The point is not to collect a quick reply. It is to aggressively filter vague answers into the fixture, defect flag, affected area, urgency and safety detail your office and technicians actually need. If the answer stays generic, the qualification stays open.

Proof — Hermia asks for specifics
Hermia keeps the conversation on one job-detail branch until the lead gives an answer that is usable.
04 — Real Scheduling (Simpro)

Booked against your actual calendar — not “we’ll call you back.”

With Simpro, Hermia checks your actual staff list and live schedule, looks across the next 20 days, then finds the closest available technician for the time the lead can do.

The result is a real scheduled activity in Simpro: the customer receives the booked time and technician details, and your crew receives a job that is already placed on the calendar.

There is no loose enquiry for an office team to re-key. The booking confirmation and the live schedule show the same outcome from the lead and dispatch sides.

05 — Site Address & Availability

The right site, the right address, the right access window.

Before a job is sent to the calendar, Hermia asks for the full work address and confirms it back to the lead. This stops an incomplete street name or a vague building reference becoming the job location.

It then asks when someone can provide access and corrects availability that falls outside your configured visit window. The booking only continues once the site and time are clear enough to schedule.

Address confirmation in action
The lead confirms the full address, then selects a real visit time that your business can actually service.
06 — Pricing

A real estimate — from your rates, not a guess.

During onboarding, you set your pricing criteria — what a defect rectification, an inspection, or a callout roughly costs at your rates. When a qualified lead describes their situation, Hermia matches it against your tiers and gives them a real figure before the job is booked. The "how much roughly?" conversation happens without touching your office — and price shoppers reveal themselves before costing you a cent of admin.

If they accept: the agreed figure is logged on the job record — no confusion when the job hits your schedule. If they negotiate: they're handed straight to the negotiation contact you chose at onboarding, and you're told they're reaching out about pricing before they contact you. The job lands in your CRM either way.

Estimate before booking
The estimate is shown before the job progresses, using the pricing rules you provide.
07 — Remove Your Competition

Once they are yours,
they stay yours.

A customer who has already spoken with Hermia has a familiar route back to your business. When the next issue appears, they message Hermia instead of searching for another contractor or emailing competing trades.

Hermia recognises the returning conversation, captures the new issue, and brings the lead back to your business with the context already connected.

Your repeat leadKnown customer. Fresh issue. Back to your business.
Familiar returnThey message Hermia, not a competitor.
New workA new issue is qualified for your business again.
Inside Simpro

One qualified lead.
Three Simpro modules, already organised.

Hermia is set up here for Simpro only. Each qualified enquiry is separated into the Customer, Custom Site and Open Lead records your trade office actually works from — so the job is usable before anyone starts retyping.

01 — Simpro Customers

The right customer,
before another record is made.

Hermia checks the customer first using the contact information provided through qualification. That means a returning property manager, landlord or homeowner is linked back to the correct Simpro customer instead of being entered again under a slightly different name.

For trade businesses, this protects customer history, billing relationships and repeat-work context. Your team can see who the customer is before they decide what needs to happen next.

CustomerPhoneEmailUrgencyBilling_EntityEstimate Amount
02 — Simpro Custom Sites

Not a loose address.
A custom site your crew can use.

Hermia places the work location into a dedicated Simpro Site record beneath the right customer. It confirms the actual site before booking so a client with multiple buildings, units or managed properties does not send a technician to the wrong place.

For trades, that keeps the address, access information and building context where the crew needs it. A new address creates a new Custom Site; an existing address stays linked to its existing site history.

Site AddressSite SuburbSite StateSite PostcodeAccess_NotesBuilding Type
03 — Simpro Open Leads

The qualified job.
Visible before your office calls.

Once the customer and Custom Site are right, Hermia creates or enriches the Open Lead with the actual trade detail: what is wrong, how urgent it is, which defect flag applies, what must be isolated, and the evidence the lead supplied.

For trades, the office can see the job context before dispatching anyone. The technician is not walking into a vague message; the lead is already a structured Simpro record with the information needed to action it.

Lead outcome

Hot, Warm and Cold.
Explained without guessing.

Booked contractor notifications

Qualified lead status, straight to the contractor.

When a booked contractor has a ready lead, Hermia sends a clear WhatsApp status alert. Hot and Warm alerts open the Docket. Cold enquiries are deliberately blocked until there is a real, complete job to hand over.

EmergencyHOT — today

Every Emergency is Hot, whether an estimate is accepted, being negotiated, or has not yet been discussed. The booked contractor receives the message immediately.

Follow-upWARM — review next

Warm status gives the contractor verified context before they open the Docket and decide the next action.

Incomplete or non-genuineCOLD — no contractor handoff

Cold enquiries stay with Hermia until qualification is complete. They do not reach the booked contractor as noise.
